newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Chevron says Nigeria gas project takes off.
newsitem.headline: Chevron says Nigeria gas project takes off.

text.p: Chevron Corp's multi-million dollar Nigerian Escravos gas gathering project has commenced production, a company spokesman said on Friday.
"Escravos Gas Project has begun operation that will lead to delivery of dry gas to domestic consumers early this month," the spokesman told Reuters.
All three major components of the project were completed by contractors and handed over to Chevron engineers who had successfully tested them ahead of full scale operation.

"Associated gas from Okan field has been put through the gas gathering and compression plant from where it will be dried and transported to an onshore plant for processing to gas liquids and natural gas," the Chevron spokesman said.

The $559 million gas project, a joint-venture between Chevron and state-owned Nigeria National Petroleum Corp (NNPC), involves gathering 165 million cubic feet of gas daily, now being flared at Escravos, near the mid-western Warri.
Warri has been hit in the past month by communal clashes involving youths of rival ethnic groups feuding over the relocation of the municipal council headquarters.
Chevron says its own operations were not affected by the clashes.
The gas project was initially scheduled to be commissioned on May 1 but Chevron officials say the formal ceremony will take place on a date convinient for the Nigerian authorities.
